evidence_type: Planning standard, research synthesis, passenger surveys and institutional case reports; not a calibrated Neihu causal estimate

sources.supports: Five defining BRT elements; cites 2015 standard. Not a 2024 certification.
Historical observed peak directional loads: Bangkok 1200, Guangzhou 27400 passengers/hour/direction; Guangzhou has passing lanes at stations. Station occupancy above 40% flagged as a queuing risk.
sources.limits: Not current ridership, not theoretical capacity, not percentage congestion relief. Single-berth simulation cannot borrow Guangzhou throughput.

sources.supports: Qualitative Guangzhou Gangding example of improved general traffic and bus capacity/speed; need assess traffic spillback and BRT impacts.
sources.limits: No quantitative causal congestion effect extracted.

sources.supports: Account for existing buses removed from mixed traffic, buses remaining, modal shift, diversions and turning traffic.

sources.title: The BRT Standard, 2024 edition
sources.supports: Minimum BRT: 3 km dedicated corridor, >=4 points for right-of-way and alignment each, >=20 across five basics. Turning restrictions and signal management matter; signal priority is less effective than turn prohibitions.
sources.limits: Minimum qualification is not gold certification or evidence of a Neihu effect.

sources.title: Social, Environmental and Economic Impacts of BRT Systems
sources.supports: Synthesis reports Johannesburg 13 minutes saved per one-way trip (10–20%); Istanbul 52 minutes per day. Also warns lane conversion may slow mixed traffic.
sources.limits: Secondary synthesis; original underlying studies not independently verified. No causal congestion reduction inferred.

sources.title: ITDP Brazil Survey Finds TransCarioca BRT Reduces Travel Times, Cuts Costs
sources.supports: December 2014 survey of 1,005 riders: mean travel time reduction 35%; former car users only 4% of riders, with 10% average time saving; >26% wait >10 minutes.
sources.limits: Institutional summary of rider survey; self-reported, no matched counterfactual. 4% denominator is BRT survey respondents, not all motorists.

sources.title: Guangzhou BRT Reduces CO2 Emissions by 86,000 Tonnes Annually
sources.supports: ITDP institutional release reports corridor motorist and bus-rider travel-time improvements of 20% and 29%, respectively.
sources.limits: Release uses “improved”; underlying interim report link returned 404. Not independently reproduced or established as a causal effect; no Neihu calibration.

unverified_sources.status: 404 after redirect on 2026-10-16. Institutional release read; linked interim report not obtained.

case_metrics.application: Passenger benefit reference only; do not apply to general traffic.

case_metrics.population: Typical Metrobüs passenger as reported by synthesis
case_metrics.underlying_reference: Alpkokin and Ergun (2012), Istanbul Metrobüs: first intercontinental bus rapid transit, pp. 58–66
case_metrics.application: Daily metric; not one-way and not a citywide congestion measure.
Do not equate passenger time savings or former-driver share with reduction of all car trips.
Institutional report only; underlying PDF unavailable; cannot be transferred to Neihu.
